title: The first refuge was Africa
hook: the first Muslim refugees were welcomed in Abyssinia

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ibn Taymiyyah, and his answer about Mardin: not peace, not war, a third kind. Your line was: read him in his age. Before you shared someone's words, did you ask when and why they said them? Day nine hundred sixty-five.

Umar ibn al-Khattab walks into his daughter Hafsah's house in Medina and finds a visitor there, a woman just back from across the sea. Her name is Asma bint Umays. When he learns where she has been, he tells her: we emigrated before you did, so we have more right to the Messenger of Allah than you. Asma doesn't laugh. She's angry. And she says she won't eat or drink until she has taken it to the Prophet ﷺ himself. Where had she been? The answer opens a new part of our road. Today's words: the first refuge was Africa.
screen: `UMAR TEASES A VISITOR.` → `WE EMIGRATED BEFORE YOU.` → `ASMA TAKES IT TO THE PROPHET.`

segments.voice: Asma had been in Abyssinia, across the Red Sea in East Africa. Years earlier, in Mecca, believers who were being persecuted had crossed that sea, and a Christian king, the Negus, had sheltered them. Asma and her husband Ja'far were among them. Before there was a Medina to go to, there was Africa. Now listen to what she says back to Umar, as Sahih al-Bukhari reports it, in paraphrase. You were with the Prophet, she tells him. He fed your hungry and taught your ignorant. We were far away, among strangers, in a land where we were hated, and all of it for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. So she goes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and tells him what Umar said. And he answers: Umar has no more right to me than you do. He and his companions made one hijrah. You, the people of the ship, made two. Two emigrations. One across the sea to Africa, and one from Africa to Medina. The Prophet counts the African years as a hijrah in their own right, not a detour. And the report adds one more detail. Abu Musa, who had sailed home with them, says that afterward the people of the ship came to Asma in groups to hear her tell it, and nothing in the world made them happier or meant more to them than what the Prophet had said. That's where the story of Islam in Africa begins: not with an army, but with refugees and a king who would not hand them over. Africa sheltered them first.
screen: `SHE HAD BEEN IN ABYSSINIA.` · `WE WERE FAR AWAY, AMONG STRANGERS.` · `YOU MADE TWO HIJRAHS.` · `THEY CAME TO HEAR HER TELL IT.` · then, large: `AFRICA SHELTERED THEM FIRST.`

segments.voice: The practice: thank a refuge. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a place or a person that sheltered you when you needed it. A grandparent's house. A friend's sofa. A teacher's classroom at lunch. A country that took your family in. A mosque, a library, a kitchen where nobody asked questions. Let it come clearly: the door, the smell, the face. Stay there for a while, and let yourself be grateful. If you pray, you can ask Allah to reward that person or that place. If you don't, simply say thank you in your head, and mean it. The bell holds the time.
Hijrah. Emigration for the sake of Allah, like the one believers fleeing Mecca made to Abyssinia, the first refuge, before Medina. Today's words.
Your line: africa sheltered them first. Today, send one message of thanks to a person or a place that once sheltered you, even if it's years late. Day nine hundred sixty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims tell the emigration to Abyssinia as the first hijrah, and the Negus's protection of the refugees is remembered in sermons and lessons about sheltering the persecuted.

original.note: Arabic: emigration, leaving one place for another for the sake of Allah.

trapdoor: what you thought: Islam's story in Africa starts with armies.
what it means: it starts with refugees, believers who crossed the Red Sea and were sheltered in Abyssinia.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of the people of the ship in Sahih al-Bukhari: one hijrah for Umar's group, two for those who went to the Negus.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4230–4231 (Abu Musa and Asma bint Umays: the people of the ship, two hijrahs)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the emigration to Abyssinia under the Negus)

notes: Story told from the hadith of Abu Musa and Asma bint Umays (Sahih al-Bukhari 4230–4231; Sahih Muslim 2502–2503); confirm numbering and the paraphrase, including Asma's oath not to eat or drink until she had told the Prophet, and 'a land where we were hated' (al-bu'ada' al-bughada').
'Years earlier' and 'the African years' are general time words; the exact length of the stay is not given, under the claims rule.
The index title and carry say 'first'; the script supports this with Ibn Ishaq's account that the Abyssinian emigration preceded the hijrah to Medina. Confirm.
Earlier days (y1 92; y3 742–744) told Ja'far's speech and the Negus's protection; this day takes the people of the ship as its angle and does not retell the court scene.
howItsDone calls the Abyssinian emigration 'the first hijrah'; confirm common usage.
Editor: removed the narrator's 'a lovely detail' editorializing; checked the hadith paraphrase against the cited reports.
